beats.text: Kodak built a digital camera the size of a toaster.
beats.note: An engineer named Steven Sasson assembled it around a Fairchild CCD sensor. It weighed 3.6 kilograms.

beats.text: It was 100 by 100 pixels, in black and white.
beats.note: That is 0.01 megapixels. The image was recorded onto a cassette tape.

beats.context: The time it took to write one picture to tape. Capturing it took only 50 milliseconds.

beats.text: You watched your photo on a television.
beats.note: A separate unit turned the tape data into a standard NTSC signal for a TV screen.

beats.text: The executives did not see a market for it.
beats.note: Sasson told the New York Times they were convinced no one would ever want to look at their pictures on a television set. The camera was never produced.

beats.text: Kodak invented it, then filed the patent and moved on.

beats.line: Ask who builds the future, and who ships it.
